header: Optimize bulk request size and compression
content:
Bulk sizing depends on your data, analysis, and cluster conﬁguration, but a good starting point is
3–5 MiB per bulk request.
Send requests and receive responses from your OpenSearch domains by using gzip compression
to reduce the payload size of requests and responses. You can use gzip compression with the
OpenSearch Python client, or by including the following headers from the client side:
• 'Accept-Encoding': 'gzip'
• 'Content-Encoding': 'gzip'
To optimize your bulk request sizes, start with a bulk request size of 3 MiB. Then, slowly increase
the request size until indexing performance stops improving.
Note
To enable gzip compression on domains running Elasticsearch version 6.x, you must set
http_compression.enabled at the cluster level. This setting is true by default in
Elasticsearch versions 7.x and all versions of OpenSearch.
